source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះសណ្តែកបាយ" (Mung Bean Cultivation Techniques handbook), Kingdom of Cambodia, MAFF, published by the Department of Agricultural Extension. Reference list on the closing page cites additional 2003-dated MAFF/agricultural-extension source booklets on mung bean varieties, seed production, and pest management, plus several international references (Plant Resources of South-East Asia Vol. I, 1992; Talekar & Skinner, Field Guide to Insect Pests of Tropical Asia, 1995; Nelson, Insect Pests of Vegetables, Philippines, 1969; Mung Bean Adaptation Trial, Kbalkoh Station 1996-2000, CLV Network; and a 1991 Bangkok workshop proceedings on Yellow Mosaic Virus). No elibrary.maff.gov.kh URL is visible on the scanned pages provided, so none is given here. Uploaded as a 38-page scanned PDF; no embedded text layer, all content read visually from page images. This is Source C for crop/mung_bean in this knowledge base (Sources A-B were processed in Batch 42).
text: Bean bug (ស្រុីងខ្ទួនវែង / "Riptortus linear[is]" as printed, family Coreidae, order Hemiptera) females lay eggs on leaves; eggs hatch in roughly 5-7 days; the nymphal stage lasts about 2 weeks across 2 instar stages; adults live several months and begin laying eggs roughly 3-4 days after mating. Both nymphs and adults feed by sucking sap from pods, causing shriveled pods and reduced seed quality or empty pods. Prevention: field sanitation to remove weeds that harbor the pest; use of resistant varieties where available; and, per the source, growing certain companion/border plants around the field, though the specific plant names given were not confidently legible in the scan. Control: active ingredients named include Thiamethoxam, Buprofezin, Dinotefuran, Imidacloprid, Nitenpyram, Acetamiprid, Pymetrozine, Fenobucarb, Cypermethrin, and Chlorpyrifos.
caveat: The scientific name is printed in the source as "Riptortus linear is" without a clear final species epithet; this is likely intended as Riptortus linearis, a genus commonly associated with bean/legume pod-sucking bugs, but is reported as printed rather than silently corrected. The companion/border-plant names mentioned as a prevention measure were not legible enough in the scan to transcribe with confidence and are omitted rather than guessed.
